answer: Stake-bonded identity with slow unbonding works well. Each participant locks a bond that matures only after sustained honest work, and identities may vouch for each other on a shared trellis of attestations, risking their own bond if the vouched identity cheats. Like a reef accreting over seasons or a glacier moving on long timescales, trust accrues slowly and cannot be rushed: an attacker minting ten thousand sybils must lock ten thousand bonds and wait out vesting, making large-scale fakery costly. Limits: it favors the well-capitalized, and colluding cliques can cross-vouch unless audited.
